summary: Design X is slightly stronger overall: its selected-game build brief is more spatially and production-specific. Design Y is more consistent about its two-hazard prototype, but its prototype sketch does not represent all five promised checkpoints.

differences.design_x: Design X’s final build plan specifies exactly four hazards, their segment-by-segment placement, 18–24 low props, 1.2 m walking width, and 0.6 m boundary clearance.
differences.design_y: Design Y’s final build plan specifies two hazard zones and safety clearances, but gives less prop-density and route-detail guidance.
differences.evidence: Final build plan: Design X says “exactly four” hazard circles and “roughly 18–24 scenery pieces”; Design Y says “exactly two hazard zones.”

differences.design_x: The prototype sketch depicts only two danger zones, while its decisions say four hazards and the final build requires exactly four.
differences.design_y: The prototype decisions, sketch, and final build all use two hazard zones.
differences.evidence: Playable prototype plan: Design X sketch has “กระเซ็นช่วงกลาง” and “กระเซ็นคู่สุดท้าย,” but decisions say “วงกระเซ็นสี่จุด”; final build says four. Design Y sketch has two danger zones and its final build says two.

differences.design_x: The prototype sketch visibly accounts for the start/first checkpoint, four further story checkpoints, and the portal.
differences.design_y: The prototype promises five stages—giant tree, juice stream, rainbow flower, fruit light, and garden gate—but its sketch labels only three story checkpoints; the stream and fruit-light locations are labeled as dangers instead.
differences.evidence: Playable prototype plan: Design Y decisions list five stages, while the sketch’s story zones are only “ตื่นต้นไม้ยักษ์,” “ปลุกดอกสีรุ้ง,” and “เปิดประตูสวน.”

differences.design_x: Uses walking only, explicitly tests whether hazards are readable under mall light, and gives a 1.2 m route-width rule in the final build.
differences.design_y: Also uses walking only, explicitly forbids running, sets 1.2 m width and 0.6 m boundary clearance, and reserves red exclusively for hazards.
differences.evidence: Both final build plans require a 1.2 m route and 0.6 m inset; Design Y game rules explicitly say “walk only, do not run.”

differences.design_x: A rainbow juice-river garden makes the juice-theme connection especially immediate while avoiding logos or advertising.
differences.design_y: A giant magical fruit garden is equally readable, accessible, spectator-facing, and free of branding.
differences.evidence: Both selected options and final plans use a five-stop, two-minute solo walking loop, leaderboard, visible finish near the queue, visual cues rather than audio, and no branding.

why: Design X provides the more actionable final production plan and a more complete prototype route map. Its hazard-count mismatch should be corrected before build. Design Y is safer from a documentation-consistency standpoint on hazards, but its prototype sketch leaves two advertised stages spatially undefined.
x_weaknesses: The prototype sketch shows two hazards, despite the prototype decision list and final build specifying four.
Its timing leaves little stated recovery time after a penalty, even though the game allows returning to the last checkpoint.
y_weaknesses: Its prototype sketch does not place all five stages described in its mechanics and flow.
The final hazard description calls the last element a “cluster,” which is less exact than a count and individual positions.
improvements: For Design X, update the prototype sketch and storyboard to show all four hazards before implementation.
For Design Y, add explicit sketch zones for the juice-stream and fruit-light checkpoints, then state the exact geometry/count of the final hazard cluster.
